title: New York City DOT's bicycle counts: the count sensors, their counts summed by month, and the bike routes with their installation dates
provider: New York City Department of Transportation, on NYC Open Data (Socrata): Bicycle and Pedestrian Count Sensors (6up2-gnw8), Bicycle and Pedestrian Counts (ct66-47at), New York City Bike Routes (mzxg-pwib)
credit: Bicycle counts and bike routes: NYC Department of Transportation, NYC Open Data
licence: NYC Open Data's Terms of Use; the datasets' licence fields are empty (checked 2026-11-09), and New York City's Open Data Law (Local Law 11 of 2012) publishes its datasets without restrictions on their use.
citation: New York City Department of Transportation (2026), Bicycle and Pedestrian Counts, Bicycle and Pedestrian Count Sensors and New York City Bike Routes, NYC Open Data, https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/ct66-47at, /d/6up2-gnw8, /d/mzxg-pwib
format: sensors.json: the sensors (id, name, lat, lon, firstdata, lastdata, travelmodes). monthly/<sensor>-<year>.json: one sensor's bicycle counts of one year summed by month by the portal (m: the month; n: the count; k: the quarter hours present; f: the flows, one each way), 15-minute counts underneath. routes.geojson: the segments of class I (protected lanes and paths) with their installation date (instdate), facility (ft_facilit), street and status.
coverage: 67 sensors, 56 of them counting bicycles, from August 2012; 21.6 million quarter-hour rows (2026-11-09). Bike routes of every class back to the nineteenth century's parkways, class I installed every year from 2013 to 2026. The monthly sums are asked one sensor and year at a time: a sum over all sensors in one request exceeds the portal's time limit.

all.description: The sensors and the protected routes; the monthly sums are fetched by data/products/street_changes.py, a sensor and year at a time
